title: Long-key IEM security under full XOR-related keys
summary: Construct an iterated Even--Mansour cipher with a master key longer than its block that beats the birthday bound against arbitrary XOR offsets of the full key.

formal_statement.body: For $n$-bit public random permutations and a master-key length $\kappa>n$, construct an iterated Even--Mansour family that is secure beyond $2^{n/2}$ queries in the adaptive bidirectional $\Phi_{\mathrm{XOR}}$ related-key experiment, where arbitrary XOR offsets act on the complete master key, or prove that no such construction exists in the stated model.

scope.domain: Iterated Even--Mansour block ciphers in the random-permutation model under full XOR-induced related-key attacks.
assumptions: The block size is $n$ and the master-key length is $\kappa>n$.
The adversary may apply arbitrary XOR offsets to the complete master key.
Construction and primitive queries are adaptive and bidirectional.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Restricted two-offset constructions achieve beyond-birthday security, including a four-round construction with a $2n$-bit key, but security under the full $\Phi_{\mathrm{XOR}}$ family remains open.

provenance.note: The CRYPTO 2015 TEM paper explicitly identifies the EUROCRYPT 2015 IEM question and states that its restricted two-offset result only partially solves the full-XOR challenge.

progress.summary: The TEM paper restates the full-XOR challenge and explains that its restricted two-offset construction only partially addresses it.
A four-round, $2n$-bit-key construction reaches roughly $2^{2n/3}$ security for a restricted two-offset related-key family, while explicitly retaining full XOR offsets as open.
